## The Numbers Tell the Story

Let's cut straight to the data: 12 wins, 2 losses, 85.7% accuracy on September 27th. When you're hitting at that clip, you let the statistics do the talking. I've broken down every single pick, every probability, and every outcome to show you exactly where our model crushed it—and where it didn't.

## Breaking Down the Confidence Levels

Here's what the data shows: our average win probability across all picks was 57.6%. The Cubs pick at 61% confidence hit. The Guardians pick at 61% confidence missed. That's baseball—and that's why we analyze thousands of data points to find edges.

## Game-by-Game Statistical Breakdown

Look at this: 50% confidence on the Nationals? Hit. 52% on the Astros? Hit. Even our lowest confidence picks converted today. The two misses—Rays at 54% and Guardians at 61%—represent exactly 14.3% of our portfolio. That's variance within expected parameters.

## The 61% Confidence Tier Analysis

Three picks hit 61% confidence: Cubs (hit), Guardians (miss), and Mariners (hit). That's a 66.7% conversion rate on our highest-confidence tier today. Over a larger sample size, we'd expect regression to the mean, but a 2-1 record at this confidence level still outperforms the baseline.

## What the Misses Tell Us

The Rays-Phillies miss at 54%? That's a coin flip with a slight edge. The Guardians-Royals miss at 61%? Still within one standard deviation of expected outcomes. I'm not making excuses—I'm reading the data. An 85.7% day isn't luck; it's statistical edge manifesting over a meaningful sample.
